rules.rule: domain is the model layer and the cleanest code in the repo. It must not depend on platform, infra, targets, RTOS or host libc. C11 with a strict Cortex-M0 compile. No mutable globals; inject ports and aggregates through constructors. Public headers compile standalone. A change here keeps the host tests and the 91-case stategrid acceptance green.

application depends on domain only. Cross-context calls go through consumer-defined ports bound once at the composition root with a void *ctx opaque handle. No device_ops tables, no driver registries, no new mutable globals. C11 with a strict Cortex-M0 compile and no host libc.

components are providers, not a second domain. core has no dependencies; protocol and services must not depend on application; only application may depend on protocol. Keep the manifest-visible dependency direction that check_components enforces. A public function without a production caller fails check_component_reachability unless the baseline names the test or host path.

infra holds SoCs, boards, drivers and RTOS adapters. No kernel types cross into application, domain or components; ports stay void *. One board per product, no device abstraction. ROM stays under the target link assert (IDIS 103 KiB). A power-safety path change needs hardware evidence or an explicit note that it is untested.

targets are product composition roots. product.yaml, not a CMake GLOB, decides which components enter the firmware. Every target needs a tests/acceptance entry; new behavior adds a case or explains why not. Keep the RAM and ROM static asserts tight; the 698 arena has 212 B slack on host, so a new buffer needs a budget change.

The checks and baselines are the gates. Do not weaken a check, a baseline entry or a self-check to make a change pass; fix the code or add a justified exception with a check= premise that fails when the premise stops holding. A new lint needs a negative probe. Keep the baselines exact (path, name, line; product, component, source).
